summary.intent: Execute Phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) across 8 plans and then run the full ship-phase workflow — verify, secure, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, and open the PR.
summary.outcome: All 8 plans executed (7 code-complete, 60-08 paused at human-action staging cutover checkpoint). Ship-phase gated at CodeRabbit fix commits at end of transcript; PR not yet pushed. SDK E2E gate caught a real ship-blocking regression in 60-05 (fixed); 7 CodeRabbit security findings fixed; security audit closed 27/27 threats.

repo: commitlint.config.js enforces `subject-no-parens`: parentheses in commit descriptions (e.g. trailing `(D-07)`) fail the `lint-pr-title` CI gate and must be stripped before push.

`cargo fmt --check` shows workspace-wide drift due to local rustfmt vs repo version mismatch — running `cargo fmt` would spuriously reformat all files. lint-staged does not run rustfmt on `.rs` files, so Rust commits land as hand-written.
gsd commit helper frequently reports `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying.

60-05's unit test for `resolveRecord` mocked `parseIpnsRecord` to include `pubKey`, masking the Ed25519 reality where pubKey is not embedded in record bytes — the SDK E2E gate was the only suite that caught this.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — PR body must be patched via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
`git push` / `git fetch` are blocked in the sandbox environment — must run with sandbox disabled.
Phase 60 requires a local dev DB wipe before strict IPNS testing (documented in 60-08 and DEVELOPMENT.md) because pre-strict unsigned records in the DB cause E2E failures.
The `gsd phase uat-passed` CLI command exists in help output but has no handler implementation.

code.finding: 60-05 removed `withCachedPublicKey` and the equal-seq enrich on the false assumption that pubKey is embedded in signed record bytes. For Ed25519 IPNS records, pubKey lives in the name (k51…) not the record protobuf — so resolve returned records with no sig fields, causing the strict client to throw fail-closed on every publish→resolve round-trip (28/89 E2E failures). Fix: serve the authoritative DB signed record (which has pubKey from the `publicKey` column) on equal-or-higher sequence.

`decode_ipns_cbor_validity` used early-return first-match, silently ignoring duplicate `Validity` CBOR keys. Its sibling `decode_ipns_cbor_data` explicitly rejects duplicates to guard against cross-language parser-differential attacks. Fixed to mirror that pattern — accumulate and reject on duplicate.

`register_device` catch-all `Err(_) => None` swallowed ALL `fetch_and_decrypt_registry` errors, treating tampered/invalid IPNS records as first-device and auto-authorizing. Fixed to bootstrap only on `SdkError::Api(ApiError::IpnsNotFound)` (concrete 404); all other errors propagate (D-08 fail-closed).

`parse_rfc3339_to_unix_secs` (the D-07 EOL/expiry boundary) had three leniencies: trailing date/time components silently accepted; day validation only checked `< 1 || > 31` so impossible dates (e.g. 2026-02-31) rolled forward to a LATER expiry via Hinnant civil_from_days. Fixed with exhausted-iterator checks and leap-aware per-month day validation.

TS resolve path skipped EOL enforcement entirely when `Validity` was not a `Uint8Array` (absent field). Rust failed-closed in the same case. Fixed to throw on absent Validity, mirroring Rust D-07 parity.
`parseCachedRecord` did not fail-closed when `publicKey` column was null/absent — it would return a record object missing pubKey. Fixed to return null (→404) when publicKey is absent.
Verify cache (D-11) was unbounded — could grow without limit under sustained load. Fixed with a MAX_ENTRIES cap and LRU-style eviction.

60-05's D-06 unit test codified the bug by asserting `signatureV2`/`data` are `undefined` on equal-seq, and mocked `parseIpnsRecord` with pubKey present (masking the real Ed25519 case). Updated test to assert the corrected strict-verifiable behavior; added regression test mocking without pubKey.

Web vault-settings sequence fallback swallowed all `resolveIpnsRecord` errors with a catch-all, preventing verification failures from propagating. Fixed to only treat `null` (true not-found) as bootstrap; errors propagate.

workflow: The SDK E2E gate is the only suite exercising real client→API IPNS publish/resolve round-trip. Unit suites mock the boundary and will miss integration regressions — this gate caught a 28/89 break that 343 unit tests missed.

The adversarial triage workflow pattern (fan out CodeRabbit findings to independent skeptic agents per finding, classify fix-now/defer-todo/false-positive) is effective for pre-ship review — correctly identified 4 false positives including pre-increment-sequence findings.

1Password SSH signing agent can wedge after many rapid commits (`op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`). Recovery: quit and reopen the 1Password desktop app or toggle SSH agent off/on in Settings → Developer.

Sequential gsd-executor subagents (vs worktree isolation) is the correct mode for security-critical phases with strict dependency ordering — trades wall-clock for correctness and clean per-plan verification.

When a post-phase SDK E2E gate fails, check whether the test harness uses deterministic (collision-prone) vs random account keys before assuming stale DB data — random keys rule out H2 collision immediately.
CodeRabbit CLI should be run locally before push; it surfaces real in-scope gaps that unit tests miss, especially in crypto/verification boundary code.

friction: 1Password SSH signing agent wedged mid-session after ~28 rapid commits, blocking all commits until the user manually restarted the desktop app.
gsd commit helper reports `commit_failed` false negatives — required `git log --oneline -1` verification after every commit to avoid double-committing.
60-05's unit test actively masked the regression it introduced by mocking pubKey into `parseIpnsRecord` — the bug was invisible to the entire unit suite and only surfaced in SDK E2E.
The SDK E2E gate required a full client+API chain rebuild (~multi-minute) to exercise the working-tree fix, with no incremental rebuild path.
CodeRabbit CLI returned 15 findings requiring a 15-agent adversarial triage workflow to properly classify — raw findings alone were not actionable without adversarial verification.
`cargo fmt --check` workspace-wide drift (rustfmt version mismatch) created noise after every Rust edit, requiring manual confirmation that touched files were not the source.
